doc.cssVarsIntro: Set these custom properties on the component (className / style) or on any ancestor, e.g. :root, to restyle it without overriding internal class names. Unset variables fall back to the global design tokens.

wc.intro: The same component as a standard custom element ({{tags}}) for plain HTML, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Solid or React. Import its entry once to register it; it uses the same design tokens, theme scopes and CSS variables as the React component.
wc.apiIntro: Generated from custom-elements.json. Attributes are kebab-case, properties camelCase; events are bubbling, composed CustomEvents.

fw.viaWebComponents: {{framework}} via Web Components (native coming soon): the examples below use the custom elements. A native {{framework}} renderer is planned, see <support>Platform support</support>.

setup.register: Register the elements and load the design tokens once, in your entry file —
setup.vueCompiler: Tell Vue's template compiler that minerva-* tags are custom elements —
setup.types: Add the {{framework}} typings: attributes, properties and events are type-checked and completed in templates —
setup.angularSchema: Allow custom elements in every component that uses them —
setup.solidTypes: Add the Solid JSX typings (on:minerva-* events and prop:* properties are typed) —
setup.htmlModule: With a bundler or an import map, import the element entry in a module script —
setup.htmlCdn: Without a build step, load the self-contained CDN bundle instead —

vue.examples: Each example is a Vue 3 single-file component (<script setup lang="ts">) using the native components of minerva-design/vue: v-model for values and open states, typed emits, slots for rich content. The live demo above it is that very component, mounted as a Vue island.
vue.api: Generated from the Vue component types (vue-component-meta). Props keep the React names; the value is v-model (modelValue), overlays use v-model:open, events are emits named like the React callbacks without "on" (onOpenChange → @open-change), and rich content goes in slots.

angular.examples: Each example is a standalone Angular component with CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA: #refs read with @ViewChild, [prop] property bindings, (minerva-event) listeners and component fields in the template. It is generated from the live custom-element demo shown above it.
angular.api: In Angular templates, bind properties with [name], attributes with [attr.name], listen with (minerva-event) (read $event.detail) and fill slots with slot="name".

svelte.examples: Each example is a Svelte 5 component (runes): bind:this refs, name={value} property bindings, onminerva-event handlers and $state in the markup. It is generated from the live custom-element demo shown above it.
svelte.api: In Svelte, name={value} sets a property when the element has one (an attribute otherwise), onminerva-event={handler} listens to an event and slot="name" fills a slot.

solid.examples: Each example is a Solid component: ref={el}, prop:name={value} property bindings, on:minerva-event listeners and signals in the JSX. It is generated from the live custom-element demo shown above it.
solid.api: In Solid JSX, name="…" sets an attribute, prop:name={value} a property, on:minerva-event={handler} listens to an event (case-sensitive) and slot="name" fills a slot.

html.examples: Each example is plain HTML with a module script: the markup is the live demo itself, the script finds the elements with document.querySelector, sets properties and listens to events.
html.api: In HTML, attributes are kebab-case (string, number and boolean values); set arrays, objects and functions as JavaScript properties; listen with addEventListener("minerva-event").

fw.unavailable: {{framework}}: this component has no Web Component yet. See <support>Platform support</support>.

native.unavailable: This component is not available in minerva-design/native yet. See <support>Platform support</support> for the React Native roadmap.
native.setup: Wrap your app once in MinervaProvider (theme, palette, design preset, locale, safe-area insets): see the React Native guide.
native.examples: Each example is a React Native component (TSX) rendered live through react-native-web in a phone frame; the same code runs on iOS and Android with Expo.
native.api: Props of the React Native component (minerva-design/native). React Native props of the underlying primitive (testID, accessibilityLabel, style...) are forwarded.
native.only: Mobile component: available in minerva-design/native (React Native + Expo) only.

hooks.title: Styling hooks
hooks.introReact: Public, stable selectors for your own CSS: data-minerva names the component, data-part a part, and the state attributes follow the shared vocabulary (see Styling & customization). Use the compound selector [data-minerva][data-part]: it also matches portalled parts. Library CSS is in @layer minerva, so unlayered rules win without !important.
hooks.introWc: Public, stable selectors for your own CSS: the tag names the component, ::part() reaches a part, and states are custom states of the host, selected with :state() (same vocabulary as the React data-* attributes; see Styling & customization).
hooks.itemsReact: Item states (a menu item, an option, a row, a day...) are attributes of the item element itself, with the same vocabulary: [data-minerva="menu"][data-part="item"][data-highlighted]. They change with the keyboard and the pointer like the ARIA state they mirror.
hooks.itemsWc: Items rendered in the shadow root expose their states as extra part names, <part>--<state>, next to the part name: combine them in ::part(), e.g. minerva-menu::part(item item--highlighted). Items that are elements of their own (<minerva-option>, <minerva-tab>...) use their own :state() instead.

item.expanded: Set on the options of the open path; never on the selected leaf at its end

item.current: The current step has no status value
item.status: complete: before the current step; upcoming: after it
item.disabled: Navigable steps only (a disabled step has no effect in read-only steps)

states.state: Open / closed, checked / unchecked / indeterminate, or active / inactive (components and items)
states.dragging: While a file is dragged over it
states.side: Side of the anchor the content is placed on
states.align: Alignment of the content along its side
states.selected: The selected item (aria-selected: option, row, day)
states.expanded: While expanded (its submenu, children or branch is open)
states.outside: A day outside the displayed month
states.sort: Sort direction of a sortable column (ascending, descending, none)
states.fill: Fill of a star (full, half, empty)

parts.arrow: The arrow pointing at the anchor
parts.content: The content panel (popup, dialog panel or main content)
parts.heading: The heading
parts.item-indicator: The check / radio mark of an item
parts.label: The label
parts.root: The outermost element of the component
parts.title: The title
parts.trigger: The trigger (not rendered with asChild: the child keeps its own hooks)
